scope: Explicit need/want/polite-request alternatives for the same sixteen assessed noun meanings across 110 directions. Updates 2,080 records and adds 320 Swahili conditional-preference constructions.

decisions.meaning: The noun meanings and exact full references from needs_frame_author_assessment_001 remain unchanged. Need, want and polite preference are deliberately different surrounding grammar; only their shared noun focus is aligned. A need sentence is never returned as the full translation of a want sentence by this extension.
decisions.bounded_forms: Explicit English need/want/would-like forms, Spanish necesitar/querer, French besoin/vouloir with concept-specific articles, German brauchen/moechten, Italian bisogno/volere with concept-specific articles, Portuguese precisar/querer/gostaria, Arabic need/want prefixes, Chinese need/want prefixes retaining classifiers, Japanese need/want/polite suffixes and Korean subject/object-particle request suffixes are enumerated. No unrestricted wildcard, stemming or generated agreement is introduced.
decisions.swahili: The assessed subject and tense slots now permit hitaji and taka roots. Separate finite subject+nge+penda alternatives cover polite conditional preference; their canonical need reference is also explicitly present to bind the unchanged noun scope. Existing full and first-person contracted present forms remain. Unassessed negative forms are still excluded.
decisions.quantity_and_ownership: More/some and articles outside the lexical focus remain in place. The available-time construction still requires the assessed quantity context. Conventional multiword noun compounds keep their existing internal links; no new ownership rewriting is authorized.
decisions.readings_and_references: All lexical readings and complete native references are byte-for-byte inherited from the pinned base authoring. Whole readings remain exact authored sentences only; these grammar alternatives do not automatically acquire a full-sentence reading or whole translation.
decisions.provenance: Extension authored from the existing request constructions and general grammar, not any inspected evaluation wording. The training-only queue informed the prior noun topic batch. Future measurements on the reused AfriWOZ probe are diagnostic, not untouched independent acceptance.
decisions.limits: Author assessment only. Native compilation, person/tense preservation, competing-noun abstention, actual translation outputs, conversational coverage and independent linguistic review remain separate gates.
